key_insight: The quadratic memory/computation bottleneck in offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction comes from a varying-length Key-Value (KV) scene representation; distilling that KV space into a fixed-size MLP via test-time training (VGG-T^3) removes the scaling bottleneck while preserving geometry.
problem_solved: Offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods scale poorly: memory and compute grow quadratically with the number of input images, preventing practical reconstruction from large multi-view collections.
method: Identify the variable-length Key-Value (KV) scene representation as the source of quadratic scaling and distill it into a compact, fixed-size MLP.
Use test-time training to fit a per-scene MLP that encodes scene geometry, replacing the varying-length KV store with a constant-size representation.
Perform offline feed-forward reconstruction from the distilled MLP, enabling reconstruction from many images without quadratic memory/computation growth.
impact: Makes offline, feed-forward 3D reconstruction practical at scale by drastically reducing memory and compute requirements; enables large photo collections and mapping pipelines to produce high-quality reconstructions on commodity hardware.

paper_title: VGG-T$^3$: Offline Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction at Scale
paper_authors: Sven Elflein, Ruilong Li, Sérgio Agostinho, Zan Gojcic, Laura Leal-Taixé
